recommendedTextbook.title: Junior English Project for Secondary Schools 2
recommendedTextbook.author: N. Grant, D. Olagoke, J. Southern

subtopics: Fundamental rule: singular subject takes singular verb, plural subject takes plural verb
Compound subjects joined by 'and'
Indefinite pronouns as subjects (everyone, somebody, each, neither, either take singular verbs)
objectives: Apply rules of basic and proximity concord in structured sentences
Detect and correct concord violations in pupil essay drafts
Score 100% on concord multiple-choice diagnostics

topics.topic: Tenses II: Present Continuous, Past Continuous and Present Perfect Tenses
subtopics: Formation of present continuous (is/are + verb-ing) and past continuous (was/were + verb-ing)
Present perfect tense: have/has + past participle for actions with present relevance
Distinction between simple past (completed in past) and present perfect (ongoing relevance)
objectives: Conjugate verbs accurately into continuous and perfect tenses
Differentiate 'I have eaten' from 'I ate' with timeline demonstrations

subtopics: Meaning of diphthongs as vowel glides within the same syllable
Closing diphthongs: /eɪ/ (play, wait), /aɪ/ (buy, night), /ɔɪ/ (boy, coin)
Centring diphthongs and word pronunciation drills
objectives: Pronounce diphthong minimal pairs distinctly without monophthong substitution
Identify correct phonetic symbols matching underlined letter combinations

topics.topic: Continuous Writing: Narrative Essay ('An Unforgettable Journey')
subtopics: Characteristics of narrative writing (chronological plot, setting, dialogue, climax)
Use of past tenses and time transitional markers (firstly, subsequently, suddenly, eventually)
Writing a 4-paragraph narrative on a journey across Nigerian highways or rail corridors
objectives: Develop an engaging narrative hook that captivates reader interest
Maintain consistent past tense throughout narrative storytelling
Punctuate direct speech dialogue with inverted commas correctly

topics.topic: Informal Letter Writing: Structure, Tone, Salutation and Sign-Off
subtopics: Features of informal letters: sender address, date, informal greeting ('Dear Tolu')
Conversational and affectionate tone, contractions allowed (I'm, don't)
Complimentary close ('Yours affectionately', 'Your friend') followed by first name
objectives: Format an informal letter layout according to WAEC/BECE conventions
Draft a letter to a friend describing experiences in Junior Secondary School 2

topics.topic: Active Voice vs Passive Voice: Sentence Transformations
subtopics: Structure of active voice: Subject + Verb + Object
Structure of passive voice: Object + form of 'be' + Past Participle + 'by' + Subject
When to use passive voice: when the doer is unknown or when the action is emphasized
objectives: Transform active sentences into passive voice without altering intended meaning
Identify passive constructions in newspaper headlines and scientific reports

subtopics: Diagnostic evaluation on concord, tenses, diphthongs, narrative writing, and voice
Targeted remedial grammar clinic
objectives: Assess pupil performance against JSS 2 curricular standards

topics.topic: Vocabulary Development: Words Associated with the Hospital and Healthcare
subtopics: Medical personnel: physician, surgeon, pediatrician, nurse, pharmacist, radiologist
Healthcare terms: diagnosis, prescription, outpatient, ward, intensive care, immunization
Register passage reading and vocabulary cloze tests
objectives: Use specialized medical vocabulary accurately in contextual sentences
Complete 10-item vocabulary register cloze passages

topics.topic: Reading Comprehension: Identifying Topic Sentences and Main Ideas
subtopics: Structure of expository paragraphs: topic sentence, supporting facts, concluding remark
Identifying stated and implied topic sentences in Nigerian socio-economic articles
Distinguishing major supporting ideas from minor illustrative details
objectives: Extract the central theme and topic sentence of each paragraph in a reading text
Write a 2-sentence summary condensing a 300-word article

topics.topic: Literature in English: Personification and Irony in African Prose and Drama
subtopics: Definition and examples of personification (giving human attributes to inanimate objects)
Definition of irony: verbal, situational, and dramatic irony
Analyzing irony and personification in assigned Nigerian junior secondary drama texts
objectives: Identify instances of personification and explain the imaginative effect produced
Explain verbal irony vs situational irony with classroom examples

topics.topic: Direct and Indirect (Reported) Speech I: Conversion of Statements
subtopics: Features of direct speech (exact words inside quotation marks)
Rules of backshifting tenses in reported speech (present simple -> past simple)
Changes in pronouns and adverbs of time and place (now -> then, today -> that day, here -> there)
objectives: Convert direct speech statements into reported speech without punctuation errors
Apply adverb and pronoun conversion rules accurately

topics.topic: Comprehensive Termly Revision & Oral Speech Testing
subtopics: Review of concord, tenses, letter writing, medical register, and reported speech
Oral reading and pronunciation evaluation
objectives: Complete JSS 2 English Studies Term 1 syllabus review

subtopics: Terminal examination and grading
objectives: Complete JSS 2 English Studies evaluation
